entries.evidence: The production process owns one Waitress HTTP server and Flask exposes POST /telegram/webhook.

entries.old_symbol: webhook secret check before request JSON decode
entries.evidence: Readiness/acceptance and hmac.compare_digest secret rejection happen before get_json/Update decoding.
Current code uses Update.de_json with the live PTB bot and rejects bool/non-int/invalid update identifiers before enqueue.
Current bridge uses thread-safe loop submission and explicitly tracks accepting/inflight/drain state.
Application initialization, transport registration, start and readiness are explicit; HTTP ingress returns 503 until acceptance is enabled.

entries.old_symbol: shutdown barrier: stop intake, drain inflight, Application.stop, save, shutdown
entries.evidence: Shutdown first deactivates ingress/readiness, drains inflight submissions, stops PTB, invokes session shutdown hook and shuts the application down while intentionally retaining the configured webhook.

entries.old_symbol: polling rollback without destructive pending-update loss
entries.evidence: Polling remains an explicit mode and removes webhook ownership with drop_pending_updates=False.
Current production composition has no InlineQueryHandler. Restoring inline_query would widen public ingress without a consumer; message and callback_query are the least-privilege set.
Value is validated in Telegram's supported range and production is deliberately serialized at one connection.

entries.old_symbol: server request envelope separate from Mini App JSON limit
entries.evidence: Render explicitly used 1 MiB server envelope and 64 KiB Mini App limit, but keep_alive.py fallback was 64 KiB while Flask fallback was 1 MiB.
entries.branch_action: Aligned Waitress fallback to the 1 MiB server envelope without changing the 64 KiB Mini App limit; regression covered.

entries.old_symbol: setWebhook fail-closed + HTTPS/public URL validation + no-store
entries.evidence: False/exception from setWebhook aborts readiness; webhook URL validation is stricter than the old PR and readiness/webhook responses are non-cacheable.
Role is derived from persisted creator/opponent identity; callback-provided role is not authoritative.
Single Mongo find_one_and_update predicates waiting state, empty opponent and creator != joiner, preventing overwrite and self-join across workers.
entries.branch_action: Added barrier/thread simultaneous-join regression proving exactly one winner.

entries.evidence: Per-participant terminal result is a durable compare-and-set with replay recognition rather than a process-local finish flag.
Final claim is durable and independently retry-safe for both participant outcomes; partial reward application is recovered from receipts.
Atomic user-document reward/stat update is guarded by a deterministic SHA-256 receipt-map key. Unlike the old 100-item receipt array, current receipts are non-evicting.

entries.current_equivalent: durable battle result outbox with per-recipient claim token/lease/ack + terminal cleanup
entries.evidence: Each participant delivery has durable ownership/ack state and final evidence is retained until both deliveries are settled.
entries.branch_action: Moved synchronous claim/list/ack/release storage boundaries off the PTB loop and retained delivery-order guards.

entries.evidence: Cancellation is participant scoped and refuses states containing durable result/finalization evidence, preserving crash recovery.
Durable recovery existed, but synchronous Mongo list/claim/maintenance calls were executed from async PTB JobQueue paths.
entries.branch_action: Offloaded Mongo operation boundaries with asyncio.to_thread; no process-local durability lock introduced; loop-responsiveness tests added.

entries.evidence: Current-user identity is part of durable lookup; ambiguous duplicate-active-session or Mongo failure raises instead of authorizing by UUID possession.
Restart is stronger: owner + expected attempt_id + exact lifecycle state CAS, creates a new attempt_id in the same durable container and recognizes only safe lost-response replay.
Cancellation requires current owner and an incomplete recoverable state; result-pending/finalizable evidence cannot be destructively cancelled.
Callback token locates an attempt; effective_user.id supplies authorization and Mongo is the authority.
entries.branch_action: Core session DB boundary additionally moved off PTB event loop.

entries.evidence: Current user and attempt_id are checked before the restart CAS; duplicate/stale callbacks cannot claim the replacement attempt twice.
entries.branch_action: Challenge and quiz persistence boundaries moved off PTB event loop.

entries.evidence: Current user is included in action resolution and terminal/pending-result states fail closed.
entries.branch_action: Persistence boundary moved off PTB event loop.

entries.evidence: Embedded target user id is explicitly compared to callback query.from_user.id before any foreign user_data access; review_nav implicitly targets the current user.

entries.old_symbol: Mongo outage fails session authorization closed
entries.evidence: Persistence ambiguity is surfaced as an error/stale response; it is never converted into authorization success or a new attempt.

wave11_current_main.finding: create_quiz_session() can return generated id after failed insert
wave11_current_main.base_evidence: Insert exceptions and duplicate-key conflicts already failed closed, but InsertOneResult.acknowledged == false was not rejected on all creation paths.
wave11_current_main.branch_resolution: Strict Telegram creation, Mini App session creation and legacy database.create_quiz_session now require acknowledged writes; exception/duplicate/unacknowledged cases are regression-tested.

wave11_current_main.finding: finish session and scoring are separate non-idempotent writes
wave11_current_main.base_evidence: Current main already uses owner/attempt completion CAS, a scoring claim state, deterministic scoring request id and a durable user score receipt before terminal session transition.
wave11_current_main.branch_resolution: No replacement transaction added; existing explicit retry-safe state machine retained.

wave11_current_main.finding: score can be credited while session remains in_progress
wave11_current_main.base_evidence: A crash may physically leave status=in_progress/result_pending with scoring_state=applied, but this is explicit recovery evidence: the receipt prevents duplicate credit and replay completes the terminal transition.
wave11_current_main.branch_resolution: Existing recovery semantics retained and exercised.

wave11_current_main.finding: finished history is subject to the same short TTL as transient sessions
wave11_current_main.base_evidence: legacy_session_retention already migrates unsafe generic TTL indexes to a terminal-only partial TTL keyed by terminal_updated_at; in-progress/result_pending recovery evidence is not put under the terminal TTL. Terminal retention defaults to 90 days and migration fails closed if unsafe scoring evidence would be lost.
wave11_current_main.branch_resolution: No duplicate startup migration retained; baseline session_integrity import already executes the migration before runtime authority is used.

wave11_current_main.finding: synchronous Mongo can block the PTB event loop
wave11_current_main.base_evidence: Core quiz, battle recovery/delivery and other async durable jobs still invoked synchronous Mongo operation boundaries directly.
wave11_current_main.branch_resolution: Latency-sensitive quiz/Challenge CAS/finalization, Battle maintenance/outbox, report acceptance/outbox and broadcast outbox boundaries now use thread offload. Startup/index hardening remains synchronous intentionally before the PTB loop. Legacy read-only presentation/admin queries remain classified responsiveness debt, not durable correctness authority.

wave11_current_main.finding: Mini App retries are result-idempotent but distinct concurrent results can both receive Daily/Challenge bonus
wave11_current_main.base_evidence: Bonus eligibility was derived from a pre-read while the persistence predicate only guarded one result_id receipt, allowing two distinct concurrent results to observe the same eligibility state.
wave11_current_main.branch_resolution: Mini App scoring now uses durable optimistic CAS against the user aggregate/receipt state shared with Telegram scoring; weekly-best projection is monotonic and duplicate-key race safe. Barrier/thread tests cover distinct concurrent result ids.
